associated_commands.intent: Test the infected machine's internet connectivity by downloading a Google logo image.
Download a batch file from APT41 infrastructure after exploiting ManageEngine Desktop Central; it installs a Cobalt Strike BEACON loader.
Run by an LNK file embedded in a Word invoice lure: download rh72.bin with BITS at high priority, save it as file.exe in %AppData% and run it.
Create a BITS job named d1f2g34 as the first step of the persistence that UBoatRAT sets up in init.bat.
Add the local file net.exe to the job to be transferred to %temp%\sys.log, so BITS has a copy to complete.
Set BITS to run the UBoatRAT copy c:\programdata\svchost.exe when the job finishes or errors, so the malware keeps running after a reboot.
Resume the job so BITS keeps executing the malware periodically, even after the computer reboots.
First of five bitsadmin commands that the LOK implant uses to issue an additional beacon to the C2 server; it cancels any existing BITS job named pdj.
Create the BITS job pdj, part of the sequence used to issue an additional beacon to the C2 server.
Set the pdj job to high priority, part of the sequence used to issue an additional beacon to the C2 server.

Add the C2 URL carrying the computer name, user name and proxy IP to the job; Kaspersky says its purpose is not entirely clear but is probably to bypass a proxy in the victim network and give the C2 the victim's IP.
Resume the pdj job so the beacon is sent, the last command of the sequence used to issue an additional beacon to the C2 server.
Upload (exfiltrate) data collected on the victim to the C2 server through a BITS upload job.
Download the legitimate AnyDesk executable onto a victim machine as a remote desktop access tool.
Deploy the Sodinokibi ransomware executable from the domain controller to remote systems.

attack_detection_strategies.name: Detection of Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol

analytics.description: Detects data access or staging events followed by outbound data flows using unencrypted protocols (e.g., FTP, HTTP) initiated by unexpected processes or to rare destinations.

attack_detection_strategies.name: Detect Ingress Tool Transfers via Behavioral Chain

analytics.description: Unusual or uncommon processes initiate network connections to external destinations followed by file creation (tools downloaded).

attack_detection_strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Lateral Tool Transfer across OS platforms

analytics.description: Correlate suspicious file transfers over SMB or Admin$ shares with process creation events (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe) that do not align with normal administrative behavior. Detect remote file writes followed by execution of transferred binaries.

attack_detection_strategies.name: Detect abuse of Windows BITS Jobs for download, execution and persistence

analytics.description: Behavioral chain: (1) An actor creates or modifies a BITS job via bitsadmin.exe, PowerShell BITS cmdlets, or COM; (2) the job performs HTTP(S)/SMB network transfers while the owning user is logged on; (3) upon job completion/error, BITS launches a notify command (SetNotifyCmdLine) from svchost.exe -k netsvcs -s BITS, often establishing persistence by keeping long-lived jobs. The strategy correlates process creation, command/script telemetry, BITS-Client operational events, and network connections initiated by BITS.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.description: Enforce proxies and use dedicated servers for services such as DNS and only allow those systems to communicate over respective ports/protocols, instead of all systems within a network.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary command and control infrastructure and malware can be used to mitigate activity at the network level.

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.description: Follow best practices for network firewall configurations to allow only necessary ports and traffic to enter and exit the network.

mitigations.name: Data Loss Prevention
mitigations.description: Data loss prevention can detect and block sensitive data being sent over unencrypted protocols.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware or unusual data transfer over known protocols like FTP can be used to mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific obfuscation technique used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions. Adversaries will likely change tool C2 signatures over time or construct protocols in such a way as to avoid detection by common defensive tools.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.description: Use network filtering to block outbound traffic from compromised systems to unapproved external destinations. Restricting access to known, trusted IP addresses and protocols can prevent attackers from downloading malicious tools or payloads onto compromised servers after gaining initial access.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Network intrusion detection and prevention systems that use network signatures to identify traffic for specific adversary malware or unusual data transfer over known tools and protocols like FTP can be used to mitigate activity at the network level. Signatures are often for unique indicators within protocols and may be based on the specific obfuscation technique used by a particular adversary or tool, and will likely be different across various malware families and versions.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.description: Consider reducing the default BITS job lifetime in Group Policy or by editing the JobInactivityTimeout and MaxDownloadTime Registry values in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\BITS.
